As of June 2026, SKU-H10 (arabica beans 1 kg) in Poland has a stock coverage of 50 months. This is in QTY_EQ (kg equivalent), on standard stock only. The stock is 5,000 against a 24-month forecast of 2,200.

- **Flag BEYOND_HORIZON:** The stock lasts longer than the 24-month forecast window. The 50 months is therefore an extrapolation: stock divided by the mean non-zero monthly forecast.
- **Warning FORECAST_GAPS_FILLED (2 months):** Two months in the forecast horizon have no forecast row. They were counted as zero demand.

Dry pasta in the United Kingdom had a stock coverage of about 2.37 months as of June 2026. That is how long the stock on hand would last against the next 24 months of forecast demand, if nothing is replenished. The figure is in months, not packs. Raw pack counts aren't supported because pack sizes differ, so stock and forecast are measured in quantity-equivalent units (kg or L). On that basis the stock was about 14,611 and the 24-month forecast about 138,399. The scope is standard items only, because bulk stock is excluded by default.

**Warning (FORECAST_GAPS_FILLED, 5 months):** Five months of the 24-month forecast window have no forecast row and were counted as zero demand. If those months have real demand, the true coverage could be somewhat lower.

Coverage is measured at one analysis month, so I can't give a single figure for the whole of 2026. Which month do you want for flour and baking (PANTRY_FLOUR) in France? The latest available month is June 2026, and 2026 months run from January to June.

I can also give a series of several months, with one coverage figure per month. Those figures can't be totalled or averaged into a yearly number.

I can't give you coverage by lifecycle status for this slice. The coverage tool refused the request (refusal code MASTER_DATA_FANOUT). At least one item in the item master data has rows marked both ACTIVE and PHASE_OUT. Any coverage figure split by lifecycle status would therefore count that item's stock or forecast more than once, so the tool returned no numbers.

The request was cooking oils (PANTRY_OIL) in Sweden (SE), June 2026, in quantity-equivalent units. The item's lifecycle status needs correcting in the item master data before this breakdown can be reliable.

If it helps, I can give coverage for cooking oils in Sweden without the lifecycle split, or split it by another attribute such as warehouse or batch status.
